Methods of Evaluation of Definite Integrals
solution:
Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\sqrt{1-\cos 4x}\ dx\)
\(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\sqrt{2\sin^{2}2x}\ .\ dx\)
\(\left(\because 1-\cos A = 2\sin^{2}\dfrac{A}{2}\right)\)
\(= \sqrt{2}\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\sin 2x\ dx\)
\(= \sqrt{2}\left[\dfrac{-\cos 2x}{2}\right]_{0}^{\pi/2}\)
\(= \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\left[\cos 2\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\cos 0\right]\)
\(= -\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\left[\cos \pi-\cos 0\right]\)
\(= -\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(-1-1) = \sqrt{2}\)
\(\therefore \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\sqrt{1-\cos 4x}\ dx = \sqrt{2}\)

subtopic: Methods of Evaluation of Definite Integrals
solution:
Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\cos^{3}x\ dx\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{1}{4}\left[\cos 3x+3\cos x\right] dx\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{4}\left[\sin 3x\cdot\dfrac{1}{3}+3\sin x\right]_{0}^{\pi/2}\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{4}\left[\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\sin 3\dfrac{\pi}{2}+3\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)-\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\sin 3(0)+3\sin (0)\right)\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{4}\left[\dfrac{1}{3}\sin\dfrac{3\pi}{2}+3\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac{1}{3}\sin 0+3\sin 0\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{4}\left[\dfrac{1}{3}(-1)+3(1)-0\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{4}\left[-\dfrac{1}{3}+3\right] = \dfrac{1}{4}\left[\dfrac{8}{3}\right] = \dfrac{2}{3}\)
\(\therefore \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\cos^{3}x\ dx = \dfrac{2}{3}\)

subtopic: Methods of Evaluation of Definite Integrals
solution:
Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/4}\dfrac{\sec^{2}x}{2\tan^{2}x+5\tan x+1}\ dx\)
put \(\tan x = t\)  \(\therefore \sec^{2}x\ dx = 1\ dt\)
As \(x\) varies from 0 to \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\)
\(t\) varies from 0 to 1
\(= \int_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{2t^{2}+4t+1}\ dt\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{t^{2}+2t+\dfrac{1}{2}}\ dt\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{t^{2}+2t+1-1+\dfrac{1}{2}}\ dt\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{(t+1)^{2}-\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{2}}\ dt\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\ \dfrac{1}{2\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}\left[\log\dfrac{(t+1)-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}{(t+1)+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\right]_{0}^{1}\)
\(= \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\log\left[\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}\,t+\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}\,t+\sqrt{2}+1}\right)\right]_{0}^{1}\)
\(= \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\left[\log\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}(1)+\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}(1)+\sqrt{2}+1}\right)-\log\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}(0)+\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}(0)+\sqrt{2}+1}\right)\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\left[\log\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}-1}{2\sqrt{2}+1}\right)-\log\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}+1}\right)\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\log\left[\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}-1}{2\sqrt{2}+1}\right)\div\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}+1}\right)\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\log\left[\dfrac{3+\sqrt{2}}{3-\sqrt{2}}\right]\)

subtopic: Methods of Evaluation of Definite Integrals
solution:
Let \(I = \int_{1}^{2}(\log x)\left(\dfrac{1}{x^{2}}\right) dx\)
\(= \left[(\log x)\int\dfrac{1}{x^{2}}\ dx\right]_{1}^{2}-\int_{1}^{2}\dfrac{d}{dx}\log x\left(\int\dfrac{1}{x^{2}}\ dx\right) dx\)
\(= \left[(\log x)\left(-\dfrac{1}{x}\right)\right]_{1}^{2}-\int_{1}^{2}\dfrac{1}{x}\left(-\dfrac{1}{x}\right) dx\)
\(= \left[-\dfrac{1}{x}\log x\right]_{1}^{2}+\int_{1}^{2}\dfrac{1}{x^{2}}\ dx\)
\(= \left[-\dfrac{1}{x}\log x\right]_{1}^{2}+\left[-\dfrac{1}{x}\right]_{1}^{2}\)
\(= \left[\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\log 2\right)-\left(-\dfrac{1}{1}\log 1\right)\right]+\left[\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)-\left(-\dfrac{1}{1}\right)\right]\)
\(= -\dfrac{1}{2}\log 2-0-\dfrac{1}{2}+1 = \dfrac{1}{2}-\dfrac{1}{2}\log 2\)  \(\because \log 1 = 0\)
\(\therefore \int_{1}^{2}\dfrac{\log x}{x^{2}}\ dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(1-\log 2\right)\)

subtopic: Methods of Evaluation of Definite Integrals
solution:
Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\cos x}{1+\cos x+\sin x}\ dx\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)-\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{2\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)+2\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\cdot\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}\ dx\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\left[\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)-\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right]\left[\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)+\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right]}{2\left[\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right]\left[\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)+\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right]}\ dx\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\left[\dfrac{\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)-\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}\right] dx = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\left[1-\tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right] dx\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[x-\log\left(\sec\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\dfrac{1}{\dfrac{1}{2}}\right]_{0}^{\pi/2}\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{\pi}{2}-2\log\left(\sec\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)-\left(0-2\log\sec 0\right)\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{\pi}{2}-2\log\sqrt{2}-0+2(0)\right] = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{\pi}{2}-2\log\sqrt{2}\right] = \dfrac{\pi}{4}-\log\sqrt{2}\)
\(\therefore \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sec^{2}x}{1+\cos x+\sin x}\ dx = \dfrac{\pi}{4}-\log\sqrt{2}\)

subtopic: Methods of Evaluation of Definite Integrals
solution:
Let \(I = \int_{0}^{1/2}\dfrac{1}{(1-2x^{2})\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\ dx\)
put \(x = \sin\theta\)  \(\therefore 1\ dx = \cos\theta\ d\theta\)
As \(x\) varies from 0 to \(\dfrac{1}{2}\), \(\theta\) varies from 0 to \(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/6}\dfrac{\cos\theta}{(1-2\sin^{2}\theta)\sqrt{1-\sin^{2}\theta}}\ d\theta = \int_{0}^{\pi/6}\dfrac{\cos\theta}{(\cos 2\theta)\sqrt{\cos^{2}\theta}}\ d\theta\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/6}\dfrac{1}{\cos 2\theta}\ d\theta\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/6}\sec 2\theta\ d\theta\)
\(= \left[\log(\sec 2\theta+\tan 2\theta)\ \dfrac{1}{2}\right]_{0}^{\pi/6}\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\log\left(\sec 2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)+\tan 2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)-\log(\sec 0+\tan 0)\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\log\left(\sec\dfrac{\pi}{3}+\tan\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)-\log(1+0)\right]\)  \(\because \log 1 = 0\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\log(2+\sqrt{3})-0\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\log(2+\sqrt{3})\)
\(\therefore \int_{0}^{1/2}\dfrac{1}{(1-2x^{2})\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\ dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\log(2+\sqrt{3})\)

subtopic: Methods of Evaluation of Definite Integrals
solution:
Let \(I = \int_{0}^{2}\dfrac{2^{x}}{2^{x}\left(1+4^{x}\right)}\ dx\)
put \(2^{x} = t\)  \(\therefore 2^{x}\cdot\log 2\ dx = 1\ dt\)
As \(x\) varies from 0 to 2, \(t\) varies from 1 to 4
\(= \int_{1}^{4}\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{\log 2}}{t\left(1+t^{2}\right)}\ dt\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{\log 2}\int_{1}^{4}\dfrac{1}{t\left(1+t^{2}\right)}\ dt\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{\log 2}\int_{1}^{4}\dfrac{1+t^{2}-t^{2}}{t\left(1+t^{2}\right)}\ dt\)
may be solved by method of partial fraction
\(= \dfrac{1}{\log 2}\int_{1}^{4}\left[\dfrac{1+t^{2}}{t\left(1+t^{2}\right)}-\dfrac{t^{2}}{t\left(1+t^{2}\right)}\right] dt\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{\log 2}\int_{1}^{4}\left[\dfrac{1}{t}-\dfrac{t}{1+t^{2}}\right] dt\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{\log 2}\left[\int_{1}^{4}\dfrac{1}{t}\ dt-\dfrac{1}{2}\int_{1}^{4}\dfrac{2t}{1+t^{2}}\ dt\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{\log 2}\left[\log(t)-\dfrac{1}{2}\log\left(1+t^{2}\right)\right]_{1}^{4}\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{\log 2}\left[\left(\log 4-\dfrac{1}{2}\log 17\right)-\left(\log 1-\dfrac{1}{2}\log 2\right)\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{\log 2}\left[\log 4-\dfrac{1}{2}\log 17+\dfrac{1}{2}\log 2\right]\)
\(\because \log 1 = 0\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{\log 2}\left[\log\dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{17}}\right]\)
\(\therefore \int_{0}^{2}\dfrac{2^{x}}{2^{x}\left(1+4^{x}\right)}\ dx = \dfrac{1}{(\log 2)}\left[\log\dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{17}}\right]\)
\(= \log_{2}\left(\dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{17}}\right)\)

Let \(I = \int_{-1}^{1}\left|\,5x-3\,\right|\ dx\)
\(\left|\,5x-3\,\right| = -(5x-3)\) for \((5x-3)<0\) i.e. \(x<\dfrac{3}{5}\)
\(= (5x-3)\) for \((5x-3)>0\) i.e. \(x>\dfrac{3}{5}\)
\(= \int_{-1}^{3/5}\left|\,5x-3\,\right|\ dx+\int_{3/5}^{1}\left|\,5x-3\,\right|\ dx\)
\(= \int_{-1}^{3/5}-(5x-3)\ dx+\int_{3/5}^{1}(5x-3)\ dx\)
\(= \left[-\left(5\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}-3x\right)\right]_{-1}^{3/5}+\left[\left(5\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}-3x\right)\right]_{3/5}^{1}\)
\(= \left[3x-\dfrac{5}{2}x^{2}\right]_{-1}^{3/5}+\left[\dfrac{5}{2}x^{2}-3x\right]_{3/5}^{1}\)
\(= \left[\left(3\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)-\dfrac{5}{2}\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^{2}\right)-\left(3(-1)-\dfrac{5}{2}(-1)^{2}\right)\right]+\left[\left(\dfrac{5}{2}(1)^{2}-3(1)\right)-\left(\dfrac{5}{2}\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^{2}-3\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)\right)\right]\)
\(= \left[\left(\dfrac{9}{5}-\dfrac{9}{10}\right)-\left(-3-\dfrac{5}{2}\right)\right]+\left[\left(\dfrac{5}{2}-3\right)-\left(\dfrac{9}{10}-\dfrac{9}{5}\right)\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{9}{5}-\dfrac{9}{10}+3+\dfrac{5}{2}+\dfrac{5}{2}-3-\dfrac{9}{10}+\dfrac{9}{5} = 2\left(\dfrac{9}{5}-\dfrac{9}{10}+\dfrac{5}{2}\right) = 2\left(\dfrac{18-9+25}{5}\right) = \dfrac{34}{5}\)
\(\therefore \int_{-1}^{1}\left|\,5x-3\,\right|\ dx = \dfrac{34}{5}\)

Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{1}{1+\sqrt[3]{\tan x}}\ dx\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\left[\dfrac{1}{1+\dfrac{\sqrt[3]{\sin x}}{\sqrt[3]{\cos x}}}\right] dx\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sqrt[3]{\cos x}}{\sqrt[3]{\cos x}+\sqrt[3]{\sin x}}\ dx\)  ... (i)
By property \(\int_{0}^{a}f(x)\ dx = \int_{0}^{a}f(a-x)\ dx\)
\(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sqrt[3]{\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}}{\sqrt[3]{\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}+\sqrt[3]{\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}}\ dx\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sqrt[3]{\sin x}}{\sqrt[3]{\sin x}+\sqrt[3]{\cos x}}\ dx\)  ... (ii)
adding (i) and (ii)
\(I+I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sqrt[3]{\cos x}}{\sqrt[3]{\cos x}+\sqrt[3]{\sin x}}\ dx+\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sqrt[3]{\sin x}}{\sqrt[3]{\sin x}+\sqrt[3]{\cos x}}\ dx\)
\(2I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sqrt[3]{\cos x}+\sqrt[3]{\sin x}}{\sqrt[3]{\cos x}+\sqrt[3]{\sin x}}\ dx\)
\(2I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}1\ dx\)
\(I = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[x\right]_{0}^{\pi/2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{\pi}{4}-0\right] = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\)
\(\therefore \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{1}{1+\sqrt[3]{\tan x}}\ dx = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\)
with the help of the above solved/ illustrative example verify whether the following examples evaluates their definite integrate to be equal to / as \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\)
\(\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{1}{1+\cot^{3}x}\ dx\) ;  \(\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sin x}{\sin x+\cos x}\ dx\) ;  \(\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sec x}{\sec x+\operatorname{cosec} x}\ dx\) ;  \(\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sin^{4}x}{\sin^{4}x+\cos^{4}x}\ dx\) ;  \(\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\operatorname{cosec}^{\frac{5}{2}}x}{\operatorname{cosec}^{\frac{5}{2}}x+\sec^{\frac{5}{2}}x}\ dx\)

Consider, \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi}x\,\sin^{2}x\ dx\) ... (i)
\(I = \int_{0}^{\pi}(\pi-x)\left[\sin(\pi-x)\right]^{2}x\ dx\)
\(I = \int_{0}^{\pi}(\pi-x)\sin^{2}x\ dx\)
\(I = \int_{0}^{\pi}\pi\,\sin^{2}x\ dx-\int_{0}^{\pi}x\,\sin^{2}x\ dx\)
\(I = \pi\int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{1}{2}(1-\cos 2x)\cdot dx-I\) ... by (i)
\(I+I = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\int_{0}^{\pi}(1-\cos 2x)\ dx\)
\(2I = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\left[x-\sin 2x\ \dfrac{1}{2}\right]_{0}^{\pi}\)
\(I = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\left[\left(\pi-\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 2\pi\right)-\left(0-\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 0\right)\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{\pi}{4}\left[\pi\right]\)  \(\because \sin 0 = 0;\ \sin 2\pi = 0\)
\(= \dfrac{\pi^{2}}{4}\)
\(\therefore \int_{0}^{\pi}x^{2}\cdot\sin^{2}x\ dx = \dfrac{\pi^{2}}{4}\)

stem: Evaluate the integral \(\int_{0}^{\pi}\cos^{2}x\ dx\) using the result/ property.
solution:
\(\int_{0}^{2a}f(x)\ dx = \int_{0}^{a}f(x)\ dx+\int_{0}^{a}f(2a-x)\ dx\)
Let, \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi}\cos^{2}x\ dx\)
\(= \int_{0}^{2\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)}\cos^{2}x\ dx\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\cos^{2}x\ dx+\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\left[\cos\left(2\dfrac{\pi}{2}-x\right)\right]^{2} dx\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\cos^{2}x\ dx+\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\cos^{2}x\ dx\)
\(\because \cos(\pi-x) = -\cos x\)
\(= 2\cdot\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\cos^{2}x\ dx\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/2}(1+\cos 2x)\ dx\)
\(= \left[x+\sin 2x\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}\right]_{0}^{\pi/2}\)
\(= \left[\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}+\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 2\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)-\left(0+\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 2(0)\right)\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{\pi}{2}+0\)  \(\because \sin 0 = 0;\ \sin \pi = 0\)
\(= \dfrac{\pi}{2}\)
\(\therefore \int_{0}^{\pi}\cos^{2}x\ dx = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\)

Let \(I = \int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\dfrac{x\,(1+\sin x)}{1+\cos^{2}x}\ dx\)
\(= \left[\left(\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\dfrac{x}{1+\cos^{2}x}\ dx\right)+\left(\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\dfrac{x\,\sin x}{1+\cos^{2}x}\ dx\right)\right]\)
The function \(\dfrac{x}{1+\cos^{2}x}\) is odd function and the function \(\dfrac{x\,\sin x}{1+\cos^{2}x}\) is even function.
\(\int_{-a}^{a}f(x)\ dx = 2\int_{0}^{a}f(x)\ dx\) , if \(f(x)\) even function
\(= 0\)  , if \(f(x)\) is odd function
\(\therefore I = 0+2\int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{x\,\sin x}{1+\cos^{2}x}\ dx\)
\(\therefore I = 2\int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{x\,\sin x}{1+\cos^{2}x}\ dx\)  ... (i)
\(= 2\int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{(\pi-x)\,\sin(\pi-x)}{1+\left[\cos(\pi-x)\right]^{2}}\ dx\)
\(= 2\int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{(\pi-x)\,\sin x}{1+(-\cos x)^{2}}\ dx\)
\(= 2\pi\int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{\pi\,\sin x-x\,\sin x}{1+\cos^{2}x}\ dx\)
\(= 2\pi\int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{\sin x\ dx}{1+\cos^{2}x}-2\int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{x\,\sin x}{1+\cos^{2}x}\ dx\)
\(I = 2\pi\int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{\sin x\ dx}{1+\cos^{2}x}-I\) ... by eq.(i)
\(I+I = 2\pi\int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{\sin x}{1+\cos^{2}x}\ dx\)  ... (ii)
put \(\cos x = t\)  \(\therefore -\sin x\ dx = +\ dt\)
As varies from 0 to \(\pi\), \(t\) varies from 1 to \(-1\)
\(2I = 2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}\dfrac{-1}{1+t^{2}}\ dt\)
\(I = \pi\ 2\int_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{1+t^{2}}\ dt\)  \(\left(\text{where }\dfrac{1}{1+t^{2}}\text{ is even function.}\right)\)
\(I = 2\pi\left[\tan^{-1}t\right]_{0}^{1}\)
\(= 2\pi\left[\tan^{-1}(1)-\tan^{-1}(0)\right]\)
\(= 2\pi\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}-0\right) = \dfrac{\pi^{2}}{2}\)
\(\therefore \int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\dfrac{x\,(1+\sin x)}{1+\cos^{2}x}\ dx = \dfrac{\pi^{2}}{2}\)
